messages:
lina: FYI — Acme Engineering has requested an org-level routing override so a subset of their traffic goes to their private cluster for compliance tests. They want header-based control + short TTL and audit trail. Can infra + console weigh in? :eyes:

shaun: Do we have an existing allowlist flow for org-level shunts? I remember a half-baked escape-hatch HMAC flow from last year.

devx-alex: We have per-tenant pins (console) but UX is clunky. No first-class approval flow or TTL UI for ephemeral overrides.

ops-jen: The HMAC escape hatch exists but it's gated to SRE only and not auditable enough for enterprise compliance. Also no easy rollback TTL.

lina: Acme specifically asked for header-based: `X-Redwood-Route: acme-private`, plus a signature header to prove it's an approved override. They want 30m TTL by default.

shaun: I'd prefer to surface this as a managed "conditional shunt" in the routing service: store allowlist entry (org_id, route, signer_key_id, ttl, created_by, audit_id). Enforce signature check at gateway.

devx-alex: For console UX: add a 2-step approval modal (request -> legal/ops approve) + show TTL and audit id. Also show active overrides on per-org dashboard with revoke button. I'll mock a wireframe.

ops-jen: Implementation notes:
1) Add DB table routing_overrides (org_id, matcher, target, key_id, ttl_expires, created_by, audit_ref)
2) Gateway validates `X-Route-Signature: sha256=<sig>` using key_id from override
3) Fallback: if signature missing/invalid, no override
4) Emit structured telemetry: override.applied, override.rejected, override.revoked

shaun: Example header pattern we can standardize:
```
X-Redwood-Route: acme-private
X-Redwood-Route-Key: key-1234
X-Redwood-Route-Sig: sha256=abcdef...
```
Gateway pseudo-check:
```
if override_exists(org, matcher) and verify(sig, key) and now < ttl_expires:
    route_to(target)
else:
    normal_routing()
```

pm-rajesh: From compliance, we also need immutable audit entries + email notifications for approvals and a CSV export. TTL is ok but must be explicit in approval.

routing-bot: PR opened: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4567 — routing override API + migration. (includes telemetry events).

devx-alex: Nice. One UX question — should console allow admins to create pre-authorized keys for a customer (so they don't have to go through us every time)? That avoids back-and-forth but is a security surface.

ops-jen: We can permit pre-authorized keys but only if created through the approval workflow and bound to an audit_ref. Keys should be JWT-like and rotated automatically.

lina: Proposed next steps:
- shaun + ops-jen: land gateway signature + verification (safety-first) — rollout behind feature flag
- devx-alex: mock console approval flow + revoke/ttl UI
- pm-rajesh: draft compliance checklist (audit export, retention)
- routing-bot: attach the PR and keep thread updated

shaun: Will add a canary that rejects missing signature to staging first, then opt-in by org. Keep telemetry tag `override.source:console|api` so we can measure adoption.

lina: Agreed. For ACME, we can provision a pre-authorized key after approval and demo the TTL.

pm-rajesh: Approvals must include justification and a link to the customer contract clause. I'll coordinate with legal.

devx-alex: I'll start a short prototype of the modal and list view. Putting sketches in Figma and will link once ready. :+1:

routing-bot: Deploy scheduled: staging @ 2024-11-06T02:30Z (feature-flagged). PR status: review requested.

lina: Thanks all — keeping this thread as the single source for the flow. If anyone needs to escalate, ping me or @shaun. :handshake:
